title: Microsoft Teams: MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI replace the Copilot meeting policy
summary: Hold for the licensing field: Microsoft's published Teams entitlement should not be presented as unknown merely because no separate requirement is published for the replacement policies. The rollout, migration behaviour and documented controls otherwise match the sources, including the disagreements between Microsoft's articles and cmdlet reference.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap specifies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The notice names Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) as its services.
claims.quote: Services: Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)

claims.claim: MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI replace the existing Copilot meeting policy.
claims.quote: The existing Copilot meeting policy is being replaced by two more specific policies:

claims.claim: MeetingAI controls the availability of Copilot, Facilitator, Intelligent Recap and other AI features in meetings.
claims.quote: MeetingAI - controls whether Copilot, Facilitator, Intelligent Recap, and other AI features are available in meetings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[1].note
claims.claim: TranscriptionWithMeetingAI controls whether transcription starts automatically when AI is turned on.
claims.quote: TranscriptionWithMeetingAI - controls whether transcription starts automatically when meeting AI is turned on.

claims.claim: The current Copilot policy combines AI availability and the requirement for a saved transcript.
claims.quote: Today, the Copilot policy combines whether AI is available in a meeting with whether a saved transcript is required.

claims.claim: The new model adds the ability to enforce Copilot off.
claims.quote: including the ability to enforce Copilot off.

claims.claim: Microsoft automatically maps existing Copilot configurations to the replacement policies in a one-time update.
claims.quote: Microsoft will perform a one-time update mapping each existing Copilot value to the corresponding MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI values

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The mapping preserves current effective behaviour rather than resetting existing policies to parameter defaults.
claims.quote: mapping each existing Copilot value to the corresponding MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI values, preserving the current effective behavior for your organization.

claims.claim: Administrators need not recreate policies for the migration.
claims.quote: Administrators do not need to recreate their policies.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference gives EnabledAllowOrganizerOverride as the MeetingAI parameter default.
claims.quote:
### -MeetingAI
| Default value: | EnabledAllowOrganizerOverride |

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference gives EnabledNoOverride as the TranscriptionWithMeetingAI parameter default.

### -TranscriptionWithMeetingAI

claims.claim: The reference warns that MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI are not fully released and have no effect yet.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The notice places the new settings under Recording and transcription and Copilot and other AI in the Teams admin center meeting policy.
claims.quote: The new settings will appear in the Teams admin center meeting policy under Recording and transcription and Copilot and other AI.

claims.claim: The notice gives Allow AI in meetings options of On, Off with organizer override, and Off without organizer override.
claims.quote: Allow AI in meetings: On / Off, but organizers can change / Off, and organizers cannot change

claims.claim: The notice gives Start transcription when AI is turned on options of On with override, On without override, and Off.
claims.quote: Start transcription when AI is turned on: On, but organizers can change / On, and organizers cannot change / Off

claims.claim: The Transcription policy remains and still controls whether transcription is allowed.
claims.quote: The Transcription policy remains available and continues to control whether transcription is allowed.

claims.claim: Who can manage AI replaces Allow Copilot and Facilitator as an organizer meeting option.
claims.quote: Who can manage AI - replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator option and determines who can turn Copilot and other AI features on or off during a meeting.

claims.claim: If an administrator turns Meeting AI off, Who can manage AI is set to No one.
claims.quote: If an admin turns Meeting AI off, this option is set to No one.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Who can use AI gives organizers more granular control over which participants can use Copilot and other AI capabilities.
claims.quote: Who can use AI - provides more granular control over which meeting participants can use Copilot and other AI capabilities.

claims.claim: Start Transcription with AI lets organizers choose whether transcription starts with AI where override is allowed.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model for this replacement of Teams meeting-policy settings is unknown.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams can be licensed as part of qualifying Microsoft 365 offerings or as a standalone SKU.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the opening licensing note with: 'Teams is licensed through qualifying Microsoft 365 offerings or a standalone Teams SKU. No separate requirement for these replacement policy settings is published.' Retain the existing Copilot add-on prerequisite distinction. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/teams-service-description. The schema requires published product entitlement to be reported separately from an unpublished feature-specific requirement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence requirement is published specifically for MeetingAI or TranscriptionWithMeetingAI.
claims.quote: Searched: MeetingAI license pricing; TranscriptionWithMeetingAI license. Read Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy parameter sections, copilot-teams-transcription, Teams Premium licensing and Teams service description; none specifies a separate entitlement for these parameters.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the supplied notice mentions a charge for the policy change.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot accepts Enabled, EnabledWithTranscript, EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn or Disabled in the cited management article.
claims.quote: | On | Enabled | ... | On with saved transcript required | EnabledWithTranscript | ... | On with transcript saved by default | EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn | ... | Off | Disabled |

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference lists only Enabled and EnabledWithTranscript for Copilot, unlike the four values in the management article.
claims.quote:
### -Copilot
This setting allows the admin to choose whether Copilot will be enabled with a persisted transcript or a non-persisted transcript.
Possible values are:
- Enabled
- EnabledWithTranscript

claims.claim: The transcription policy is managed in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription.
claims.quote: You can use the Recording & Transcription section in the Teams admin center or the -AllowTranscription parameter ... to manage your transcription policy.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription <$true|$false> controls transcription permission.
claims.quote:
### -AllowTranscription
Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit.

claims.claim: An administrator UI control corresponding to AllowIntelligentRecap is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowIntelligentRecap admin center turn off. Read intelligent-recap-without-saving-transcripts and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. The documented admin disable operation is PowerShell; the article's UI procedure controls expiration, not availability.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -AllowIntelligentRecap $false is the documented command for turning off intelligent recap.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -AllowIntelligentRecap $false

claims.claim: The management article says disabling intelligent recap affects all meetings, with or without saved transcripts.
claims.quote: Turning off intelligent recap disables intelligent recap for all meetings, regardless of whether transcripts are saved.

claims.claim: The article says disabling intelligent recap makes the related settings unavailable in Teams.
claims.quote: Turning off intelligent recap disables intelligent recap for all meetings, regardless of whether transcripts are saved, and the related settings are unavailable in Teams.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference still marks AllowIntelligentRecap as not fully released and without effect, disagreeing with the management article.
claims.quote:
### -AllowIntelligentRecap
This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect. Controls whether Intelligent Recap is allowed for the user's meetings.

claims.claim: Work IQ transcript access is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting settings > Transcript API access > WorkIQ access.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings. Under Transcript API access, turn the WorkIQ access toggle On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -EnableWorkIQTranscriptAccess $true -Identity Global enables Work IQ real-time transcript access.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -EnableWorkIQTranscriptAccess $true -Identity Global
This parameter requires the latest version of the Teams PowerShell module.
claims.fix: Append to controls[3].note: 'The PowerShell parameter requires the latest version of the Teams PowerShell module.'

claims.claim: Work IQ transcript access is off by default.
claims.quote: Work IQ access is also off by default.

claims.claim: Work IQ access is an organization-wide control over whether agents and apps receive real-time meeting transcripts.
claims.quote: The organizer's organization decides. Work IQ uses the setting of the organization that organized the meeting, not the setting of the app's organization or of the user the app acts for.
